top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is an invention with a clear, separable mechanism (equal light shift for both clock levels, so thousands of neutral atoms are held without Stark or motional shifts) and a verified, independently reproduced result at the 10^-18 level (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST). It opens new measurements such as relativistic geodesy and tests of constants. Credit separates cleanly into Katori (concept and first strontium lattice clocks) and Ye (record accuracy, stability and the many-body clock), and a citation tied to the lattice concept and many-atom realisation does not read as a third clock prize after 2005 and 2012. Remaining doubts (adjacency to earlier prizes, no fundamental-physics signal yet, credit for Ludlow, Lemke, Hinkley, Bloom, Takamoto and others) are real but not disqualifying, so an award is preferable to no award.
